The Chongqing and Hong Kong authorities announced today (14 October) the launch of the Chongqing-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform (CQ-HK DVP).

As set out in “The Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address”, this new cross-boundary data validation mechanism jointly established with Chongqing is one of the measures for encouraging the orderly flow of financial elements between the Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) facilitated the establishment of the CQ-HK DVP1 together with authorities including the People’s Bank of China Chongqing Municipal Branch, the Office of the Financial Commission of the Chongqing Municipal Committee, the Office of the Cyberspace Affairs Commission of the Chongqing Municipal Committee, and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the Chongqing Municipal People’s Government.

Leveraging blockchain technology and data coding (i.e. hash values), the CQ-HK DVP enables the verification of data presented by customers without involving the cross-boundary transfer or storage of the original documents. The relevant innovative technologies and mechanism have been successfully applied and proven to be stable and effective via the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform2.

The CQ-HK DVP will mainly support cross-boundary financial use cases at the outset.

The CQ-HK DVP will further foster secure and efficient cross-boundary data flow between Chongqing and Hong Kong.

items.source_excerpt:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), as representative of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government (HKSAR Government), published today (9 October) a tentative issuance schedule for institutional Government Bonds (GBs) to be offered under the Infrastructure Bond Programme (IBP) and Government Sustainable Bond Programme (GSBP) for the six-month period from October 2026 to March 2027 (Annex 1). The GBs are denominated in Hong Kong dollars (HKD) and renminbi (RMB) and will be offered by way of competitive tendering. The tentative issuance schedule contains information on, among others, the tentative tenors, tender dates, issuance sizes, issue dates and methods of issuance of individual GB issues. Further details are set out in the Information Memorandum published on the Hong Kong Government Bonds website, https://www.hkgb.gov.hk.

The HKMA also re-appoints 13 financial institutions as Primary Dealers under the institutional part of the IBP and GSBP to assist in the implementation of the GB tenders (Annex 2). Primary Dealers are also expected to provide two-way bid-and-offer quotations in the secondary market to facilitate GB trading. The latest appointment of Primary Dealers covers the two-year period from October 2026 to September 2028.

The information contained in the tentative issuance schedule, such as the tenors, tender dates, issuance sizes, issue dates and methods of issuance are tentative.

A revised issuance schedule may be issued where appropriate.
